The portable entertainment system comprises a base unit and a remote computing device. The base unit includes a processing module having a central processing unit electrically connected to a graphics processing unit. Similarly, the remote computing device includes its own processing module, which has a central processing unit electrically connected to a graphics processing unit.

When the base unit and the remote computing device are electrically connected, the central processing unit of the base unit is coupled to the central processing unit of the remote computing device. In this connected state, the graphics processing unit of the base unit remains active, while the graphics processing unit of the remote computing device is inactive.
outputs.L4:
A portable entertainment system includes a base unit and a remote computing device that can operate separately or in a connected configuration. The base unit contains a central processing unit (CPU) and a graphics processing unit (GPU) coupled to one another, while the remote computing device likewise contains its own interconnected CPU and GPU. When the remote computing device is disconnected, its CPU and GPU may operate together to provide portable computing and entertainment functions.

When the remote computing device is connected to the base unit, a communication interface couples the CPU of the remote device to the CPU of the base unit, allowing the two processors to exchange data and coordinate system operations. In this connected state, the GPU of the base unit remains enabled and performs graphics-processing tasks for the combined system. The GPU of the remote computing device is disabled, powered down, or otherwise prevented from performing redundant graphics operations.

This arrangement centralizes graphics processing in the base unit while retaining the processing resources and functionality of both CPUs. By avoiding simultaneous operation of both GPUs, the system can reduce power consumption, heat generation, and unnecessary duplication of graphics workloads. The architecture therefore supports efficient transitions between portable use and a docked or connected entertainment mode.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a portable entertainment system with a base unit and remote computing device, each containing electrically connected CPUs and GPUs, where connecting the devices couples their CPUs, activates the base GPU, and deactivates the remote GPU.
counterfactuals.output: A portable entertainment system includes a base unit and a remote computing device selectively connectable to the base unit. The base unit includes a first central processing unit electrically connected to a first graphics processing unit, and the remote computing device includes a second central processing unit electrically connected to a second graphics processing unit. When the remote computing device is connected to the base unit, an interface couples the first central processing unit to the second central processing unit to enable coordinated processing and data communication. In response to the connection, the first graphics processing unit of the base unit is activated for rendering entertainment content, and the second graphics processing unit of the remote computing device is deactivated. When disconnected, the remote computing device may operate independently using the second central processing unit and the second graphics processing unit.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an invention in formal patent language involving a docked portable gaming device that relies on the base unit’s graphics processor when connected.
counterfactuals.output:
**Title:** Portable Gaming Apparatus Utilizing Dock-Based Graphics Processing

**Abstract**

A gaming system includes a portable gaming device and a base unit configured to removably receive the portable gaming device. The portable gaming device includes a display, a first processor, and a first graphics processor operable to render interactive content while the portable gaming device is operated independently of the base unit. The base unit includes a second graphics processor having greater graphics-processing capability than the first graphics processor. Upon establishment of a communication link between the portable gaming device and the base unit, execution of at least a portion of a graphics-rendering workload is transferred to the second graphics processor. Image data generated by the second graphics processor is output to an external display and/or transmitted to the portable gaming device for presentation on the display thereof. Upon disconnection, the graphics-rendering workload is returned to the first graphics processor while maintaining an active application session.

**Detailed Description**

In one embodiment, the portable gaming device comprises a housing, a user input assembly, a display panel, system memory, a central processing unit, and an integrated graphics processor. The portable gaming device is operable in a standalone mode in which the integrated graphics processor renders graphical output based on application instructions executed by the central processing unit.

The base unit comprises a docking interface, a power supply, a discrete graphics processor, graphics memory, and one or more display-output interfaces. The docking interface may include a wired high-bandwidth interconnect configured to carry graphics commands, application data, rendered image data, input signals, synchronization information, and electrical power.

A connection manager detects coupling of the portable gaming device to the base unit and determines whether the discrete graphics processor is available for workload execution. In response to such determination, a graphics allocation controller establishes an enhanced-performance operating mode. In the enhanced-performance operating mode, graphics commands, geometry data, textures, shader instructions, or other rendering information are communicated from the portable gaming device to the discrete graphics processor of the base unit. The discrete graphics processor renders one or more image frames at a resolution, frame rate, or graphical quality exceeding that available in the standalone mode.

Rendered frames may be supplied directly from the base unit to an external display. Alternatively, rendered frames may be encoded or otherwise transferred to the portable gaming device for display on the portable device. The system may further divide rendering operations between the respective graphics processors, such that one graphics processor performs scene rendering while the other performs image scaling, frame generation, post-processing, display composition, or user-interface rendering.

When decoupling is detected, the system preserves application state and reallocates the graphics workload to the integrated graphics processor. Rendering parameters may be adjusted during the transition to accommodate the processing capability and power limitations of the portable gaming device, thereby permitting continued execution without restarting the application.

**Illustrative Claims**

1. **A gaming system comprising:**  
   a portable gaming device including a display, a first processor, and a first graphics processor configured to render interactive graphical content in a standalone operating mode; and  
   a base unit configured to removably couple to the portable gaming device, the base unit including a second graphics processor;  
   wherein, in response to coupling of the portable gaming device to the base unit, at least a portion of a graphics-rendering workload associated with the interactive graphical content is transferred from the first graphics processor to the second graphics processor.

2. The gaming system of claim 1, wherein the second graphics processor has a greater graphics-processing capability than the first graphics processor.

3. The gaming system of claim 1, wherein the base unit outputs image frames rendered by the second graphics processor to an external display.

4. The gaming system of claim 1, wherein image frames rendered by the second graphics processor are transmitted to the portable gaming device and presented on the display of the portable gaming device.

5. The gaming system of claim 1, wherein, in response to decoupling of the portable gaming device from the base unit, the graphics-rendering workload is reassigned to the first graphics processor without terminating an active gaming session.

6. The gaming system of claim 1, wherein the first and second graphics processors concurrently perform respective portions of the graphics-rendering workload.

7. The gaming system of claim 1, wherein the base unit supplies electrical power to the portable gaming device while the portable gaming device is coupled to the base unit.

a handheld unit including a first central processing unit, a first graphics processing unit, a display, and a first communication interface; and

a base unit configured to removably receive the handheld unit, the base unit including a second central processing unit, a second graphics processing unit, a video output, and a second communication interface configured to communicate with the first communication interface when the handheld unit is docked with the base unit;
